issues.description: The deletePerson method has mismatching parameter types across artifacts. The problem statement and REST design expect deletion by personId (UUID) via DELETE /persons/{personId}. The template's PersonService defines deletePerson(UUID personId), but the solution's PersonService defines deletePerson(Person person). At the same time the solution's PersonResource calls personService.deletePerson(personId) (passing a UUID). This inconsistency (UUID vs Person) will confuse students and lead to compilation errors or unclear guidance about which signature to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the deletePerson signature consistent across template, solution, and REST resource. Prefer keeping deletePerson(UUID personId) in PersonService to match the DELETE /persons/{personId} endpoint and PersonResource. Alternatively, if you want PersonService.deletePerson(Person), update PersonResource to resolve the Person before calling the service, but the simplest fix is to add or keep a deletePerson(UUID personId) method in PersonService and have it perform the removal (or provide an overload that accepts Person).

issues.description: The conceptual operation 'delete person by ID' is named and typed inconsistently across artifacts. The problem statement and the REST resource expect deletion by a UUID personId (DELETE /persons/{personId}). The template's PersonService defines deletePerson(UUID personId) (remove by id). In the solution, PersonResource still calls personService.deletePerson(personId) but PersonService was changed to deletePerson(Person person) (taking a Person object). This mismatch between using a UUID parameter vs. a Person parameter for the same delete operation breaks the conceptual mapping (and leads to a compile/runtime inconsistency).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the delete-person API consistent: restore PersonService.deletePerson(UUID personId) (as in the template and problem statement) and implement it to remove the person by id (persons.removeIf(p -> p.getId().equals(personId))). Alternatively, if you intend to accept a Person object, update PersonResource to pass a Person instance. Prefer keeping the UUID parameter to match the REST endpoint DELETE /persons/{personId}.
